name: Casa Poli
note: No Commons files. Massing is clear (concrete cube on the Coliumo cliff edge) but the size and placement of its irregular deep window openings could not be confirmed: ArchDaily, Arquitectura Viva, archiweb and the architects site were unreachable from here and search summaries disagree. Drawing the openings would mean guessing.

name: Casa de Huéspedes Ilustres de Colombia
note: No Commons files at all. Sources (via search summaries only) say brick and limestone enclosures linked by courtyards and water channels inside the ruins of the Manzanillo fort; nothing gives the elevation, roof forms or heights, so a drawing would be a guess. Its features line also says coral stone, which these sources do not confirm.

name: Cultural Foundation
note: No free photo on Commons (Qasr al-Hosn category has none that name it). Sources confirm only three wings around a central courtyard and glazed-brick-tiled arcades; not enough to draw heights, arch rhythm or elevations without guessing. (The en.wikipedia stub says it was demolished, which is outdated: it was renovated by CEBRA and reopened in 2018.)

name: Dakar International Fair
note: No Commons files (searched FIDAK, CICES, Foire internationale de Dakar). Sources agree on a triangular module on a 10 x 10 m base and seven regional pavilions around an entrance pavilion, but none give pavilion heights, roof profile or facade layout. Architect credit also varies (some add Fernand Bonamy).
